sections.text: Arjuna asked: My Lord! Viwaswana was born before Thee; how then canst Thou have revealed it to him?
Lord Shri Krishna replied: I have been born again and again, from time to time; thou too, O Arjuna! My births are known to Me, but thou knowest not thine.
have no beginning. Though I am imperishable, as well as Lord of all that exists, yet by My own will and power do I manifest Myself.

We had been discussing chapter four, Gnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga Yoga of Renouncing actions in Knowledge. So so far we have learnt in Bhagavad Gita that the sole goal of any being is happiness. And happiness we have seen is defined as absence of unhappiness. As long as there is unhappiness somewhere, I cannot be happy. Just like as we have seen, the cold is defined as absence of heat is cold. Darkness is defined as absence of light is darkness.
Happiness is defined by lack of unhappiness. So my true nature is actually happiness. But the infusion of unhappiness creates this state which I call going back from happiness to unhappiness. When there is no unhappiness, I am happy. But if even one thing is wrong, no matter how many other things are going well in my life, it just wont let me focus on the good.
In Sastra its called Kakadrasti. A crow is flying over a garden and everything is beautiful underneath. But the crow is not focusing on the beautiful flowers. He is focused on a carcass lying in that garden. Thats where he goes. So our Kakadrasti --
We dont focus on what is right in our life, we focus on what is wrong in our life. So we have to get out of this habit of seeing what is not right in my life. So what we try to do is keep searching for happiness rather than avoiding unhappiness. The search of happiness leads us to believe that my actions will get me to happiness. So we act in this world to achieve happiness which is already with us. But these actions also lead me to results which are unhappiness.
So therefore we have seen in last chapter, Arjunas question is Atha KE na prayuk toyam Papam Charati Purusha. There is no one in this life who really wants to become unhappy. And still we end up becoming unhappy by our own actions. So actions are at the root cause of whether Im happy or unhappy. Therefore we need to understand what actions are all about. The one thing we learnt is I cannot live without actions, because action is the very nature of my own being.
Nature is part of Prakriti. It is one of the attributes of Prakriti is action Rajas. And as I am part of Prakriti, as this body, mind, intellect is part of Prakriti, action is a very signature of my being who I am. So actions I cannot avoid thats given. Now, how can I avoid actions which give me unhappiness? Well, when I am performing actions, there is not a single action I perform because I want to be unhappy.
Well, let me do something that makes me unhappy. Lets see how it feels. There is no curiosity about unhappiness. I really dont want to know. But I still end up being unhappy. Thats because Im not understanding what actions are all about.
So we learnt in chapter three what actions are all about. The first thing we learnt is Yajnaarthaat Karmano, Nyatra Loko Yam Karma, Bandanaha. All actions are binding. If they are not performed for the Yajna, for the spirit of common good, then they are binding. If I am doing it for myself, they are binding. When those actions are binding, Ill be bound by the results.
In a sense, I really dont know what the results would be. They may come back as conducive results and Ill be happy or they come back as unconducive results and Ill be unhappy. So now I am in a conundrum. I want to act because thats whats going to make me happy. But also Im not quite confident that my actions will make me happy. Because I have no control over my actions.
So there got to be a way to get out of this conundrum of acting and reacting and then acting again. So Bhagavan said yes, there is a yoga, the Yoga of Knowledge. Once the knowledge takes place that I am not the actor, you will be released from this bondage of actions. Because you are not performing the actions, you cannot be bound by it. So that is Gnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga. Yoga of renouncing actions in knowledge.
When knowledge takes place that I am not the actor. Guna Gunesuvartantaha Ithimatva na Sajjadhai. We learned that in chapter three. Once I figure out that the actions are only taking place at the Prakriti level -- by my qualities, qualities of my body, mind and intellect, and qualities of the rest of the universe -- when they come in contact with each other, they react with each other. Like hydrogen and oxygen: when they are two independently standing, there is no water.
When they come together, they create water. We also work in this world the same way. By ourselves we are not reacting to anything. As soon as we come in contact with another being or an object, we react. There was sometimes we had good chemistry with him. What do you mean good chemistry?
I like him with no reason. Guna Gunesuvaratanta. I detect Gunas in him or her. Maybe a physical, mental, intellectual, something which I like. I tell people how I got into hotel designing business. Very first limited hotel.
I had designed full service hotels in my life before I came to Virginia. But then I was looking for some work. Somebody says there is an Indian community. They design lot of mid level hotel. He said no, no, youre a big time, not small time. So the first guy they introduced me was in Charlottesville.
They said, How about you come down here? Because one thing I figured out: I can win people over if Im in front of them -- on the phone and in writing its harder. But if Im in front of him I can probably have a better chance. So I go down there, talk to the guy, and then he said, Where are you from? I said Surat.
My parents actually come from Randeh. Oh, where is Randeir? In the end of the day, we never talked about what I know about architecture. They said, You are my architect now because your ancestors come from Randir. Let the architecture sort out by itself. You are my architect.
Something we find common. So therefore these actions are all bound by Gunas. But we consider it to be ours. The Bhagawan said that one who is understanding this he will not be attached to his actions. He doesnt get attached. But how do I get to that point that I dont get attached.
I have to have knowledge who I am. So this chapter starts with Bhagavan said that I taught this yoga to Vivaswan. Then the Viva swan taught to Manu. Then Manu taught to Iksvaku. And thus by lineage the knowledge was passed on to generation to generation. But now because the long time has passed the knowledge is lost.
When were Vivaswan and Manu alive? And you are now telling me that you taught them? We have discussed that Vivaswan and Manu, from a genealogical point of view, are Krishnas ancestors. Vivaswans son was Manu, who at the time of Pralaya saved his family and seven Rishis. Manus son was Ikswaku. So Vivaswan taught his son Manu.
Manu taught his son Ishvaku. And Isvaku, we know, is Ramas ancestor who established the kingdom in Ayodhya. Somewhere about 36 generations later, Rama comes. One of them was also the ancestor of Krishna. Somewhere in the 60th generation, Krishna comes. So Arjuna is saying: you are telling me that you taught all your ancestors?
So then Bhagavan said Bahuni me Vyati Thani Janmani Stavacharjuna Tani Aham Veda Sarwani Natvam Vedaparam Tapa. This is not the only life that you and I know, Arjuna. You know me in this life as Krishna. But I have taken so many births before and so did you. The only difference is I know them all. This is a very bold presentation of concept of reincarnation.
It was not that it was not introduced before. It was introduced in chapter 2. Vasamsi Jinini Yatavi Haya Navani Guru Nathi Naroparani we have already seen that this self is immutable, imperishable. It just takes one state of existence to another depending on. We know from our study of Bhagavadya by Karma actions. Our actions create experiences in this world.
These experiences create tendencies. These tendencies create likes and dislikes and desires. And to fulfill those desires we take a next state of existence. My desire was to become a rock star. Then obviously I learned music and then march on that path. So desire leads us to where we are today.
But you see, we wont remember how we got here. The one who is very aware of this transitory nature of things, he will remember all of them. See, some of us are very good at remembering dreams. All of us remember dreams, right? Some of my dreams, even ones I had in childhood, I still remember. They either still scare me or still fascinate me.
But I dont remember all my dreams. If I was more aware and enlightened about keeping myself connected to my dream world, then I would remember all my dreams. See, right now Im only connected to my waking world, and sporadically Im connected to my dream world. So I remember some dreams here and there, but not all of them. In the waking world, I think I remember everything. Then somebody says, But Rajan, you did this?
No, I dont remember. I forget almost everything she says I did. She said, You did this for some reason. Women are very historical. They remember everything. From the day I met Meena till today, she remembers everything that I did not do right.
And I dont remember any of that. But you remember what she didnt do, right? So we have very, what you call it is a convenient memory. But at least Im connected to the waking world. If Im disconnected, then I will have to have a psychiatric evaluation because I dont remember who I am and all the good stuff. Now imagine: if Im connected to the waking world, and if Im also connected to my dream world, and then also my deep sleep, then I will remember everything.
But for that I have to be a third party, not involved in it. Imagine there is a recording device which is recording everything going on in my brain. It will record everything. See, thats why when we see some recordings of our own childhood, we get fascinated. Did I look like that? So we have a memory which is very specific to time and space.
The time and space we are in. This is what remember as the reality. But if there is some way we can connect all our realities then we will have a complete view. Bhagawan said that you and I both have the capability to know that. But ignorance about who I am has created a smaller memory. The more I identify with the localized situation,
the more I will forget about my greater situation. Some of my friends still write me every year, and I have forgotten most of them, because my nature is to identify with wherever I am now. Im in Richmond. These are my friends and my family. The more I identify with Richmond, the more Ill forget my friends in Northern Virginia and Houston and Nairobi and Zambia and India. But some people remain connected because they never fully belong to where they are.
They may ask somebody and say, what are you doing? We go to Northern Virginia every weekend. We have all our friends there. They are not connected here, they are more connected there.

When Arjuna questions how Krishna could have taught Vivaswan who was born ages before, Krishna reveals a profound truth: Many births have passed for Me and for you, O Arjuna. I know them all, but you know them not (bahuni me vyatitani janmani tava charjuna). This teaching on reincarnation invites us to consider the continuity of our existence beyond this single lifetime. Just as we remember some dreams vividly while forgetting most, our connection to past experiences depends on our level of awareness. Krishna, being fully aware, remembers all; we, identified with our limited selves, remember only fragments.
The key distinction Krishna makes is that while we take birth compelled by unfulfilled desires (vasanas), He manifests by His own free will (atma-mayaya), presiding over His own Prakriti. Though unborn (ajo) and imperishable (avyayatma), He appears in creation by choice, not compulsion. This teaches us that our bondage comes from identification with limited circumstances, while liberation comes from recognizing our true nature as the unchanging witness.
Today, reflect on your patterns of attachment and desire. What recurring themes appear in your life that might point to deep-seated tendencies (vasanas)? Practice expanding your sense of identity beyond your current circumstances. Just as people who keep connected to friends from different cities never feel fully local anywhere, consider: are you so identified with your present situation that you have forgotten your larger Self? Try maintaining awareness of yourself as the witness who observes all experiences rather than the one caught up in them.
